name: Kinyarwanda
notes: Kinyarwanda (Rwanda national language). Bantu language. Prenasalized consonants are single phonemes. High tone vs. low tone — not marked in standard orthography. C/CY = /tʃ/; SH = /ʃ/; NY = /ɲ/. Grapheme table checked against Kimenyi (1980): no discrepancy found. STRESS EXEMPTION: Kinyarwanda is a Bantu tone language (lexical/grammatical high vs. low tone, per Kimenyi 1980), not a stress language in the sense this project's `stress` schema targets; word-level prominence is predictable from mora count/penultimate-lengthening but tone itself is unmarked in the standard orthography (as already noted) and is out of scope for the `stress` block, so no `stress` block is added.

sources.author: Kimenyi, Alexandre
sources.title: A Relational Grammar of Kinyarwanda
sources.publisher: University of California Publications in Linguistics, vol. 91. University of California Press
sources.notes: Reference grammar used to verify the grapheme table (prenasalized consonants, c/cy, j/jy, sh, ny) and to document the tone-vs-stress distinction underlying this spec's stress exemption.
